messages.subject: [statnet_help] setting attributes of a single edge
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] setting attributes of a single edge
messages.body_plain:
hi folks,

   Ok, maybe this is a stupid question, but if I want to set an 

attribute of an edge between vertices i and j is the only way to do 

it:



set.edge.attribute(myNetwork,"myAttribute",value=myValue,get.edgeIDs(myNetwork,i,alter=j))





I realize that it is a complicated operation because there may be 

directed and/or multiple edges between i and j, but maybe we should 

have a basic default form?  It is confusing when you can assign to 

all edges with



  myNetwork%e%"myAttribute" <- myVal



Something that uses the same conventions as the myNetwork[i,j] 

assignment?  Or maybe we just need to add an example and some more 

explanation to the attribute methods man page.  The edge ID lookup 

makes sense once you understand it, but it isn't clear from looking 

at the man for set.edge.attribute how you can discover the edge ids.



thoughts?



best,

   -skye



P.S.  maybe we should also add an example and a "see also" for 

get.edge to the main network man page.  It is a little hard to find 

without looking through the whole package listing.

messages.body_plain:
As Mark pointed out, this is an internal development question.  However, 

I will cc: the response to statnet_help, since I suspect that some of 

the folks there will find some of this to be of use.  In general, 

development questions should be kept out of statnet_help, to avoid 

deluging everyone with a lot of inside baseball.  :-)



Skye Bender-deMoll wrote:

> hi folks,

>   Ok, maybe this is a stupid question, but if I want to set an attribute 

> of an edge between vertices i and j is the only way to do it:

> 

> set.edge.attribute(myNetwork,"myAttribute",value=myValue,get.edgeIDs(myNetwork,i,alter=j)) 

> 



That's the direct way, but not the only way to accomplish this.



> 

> 

> I realize that it is a complicated operation because there may be 

> directed and/or multiple edges between i and j, but maybe we should have 

> a basic default form?  It is confusing when you can assign to all edges 

> with

> 

>  myNetwork%e%"myAttribute" <- myVal

> 

> Something that uses the same conventions as the myNetwork[i,j] 

> assignment?  Or maybe we just need to add an example and some more 

> explanation to the attribute methods man page.  The edge ID lookup makes 

> sense once you understand it, but it isn't clear from looking at the man 

> for set.edge.attribute how you can discover the edge ids.

> 

> thoughts?

> 



Well, I am sure that it wouldn't hurt to add more docs to the man page 

re: dealing with edge IDs.  You are correct that they are needed because 

of multiplex networks (since there is no other way to keep track of 

which edge is which)....their usage can be a bit arcane, and it is 

possible that the current documentation does not provide enough detail 

on the matter.  I'll add that to my TODO file for the next release.



That said, I should note that you do not have to use the long-form 

syntax to achieve this goal in most settings.  The syntax



g[i,j,names.eval="boo"]<-val



will assign val to an attribute named "boo" for every i,j edge in g.  By 

default, this will not add new edges to the graph, although this 

behavior can be changed using the add.edges argument.  (See the 

network.extraction man page for details.)  This syntax can be adapted in 

the usual manner to, say, set values for all edges incident upon a given 

vertex, and so forth.  I suspect that this will solve your problem.



> P.S.  maybe we should also add an example and a "see also" for get.edge 

> to the main network man page.  It is a little hard to find without 

> looking through the whole package listing.



I like Mark's "getting started" page for statnet...it seems to me that 

something of that form might be added for the next release.  Such a page 

would be the appropriate spot for pointers of the form you suggest.



Again, apologies to the statnet_help folks for the development 

discussion (though I think that some will appreciate the names.eval 

trick).  Follow-ups should go off-list.



Enjoy,



-Carter

messages.body_plain:

I'm attaching my network as an R-image.

It has 105 nodes and 1337 edges (density=0.245), and is named ta2.

when i run:

ta_plain<-ergm(ta2~edges)

the resulting coefficient is -2.062.

Turning this into a probability:

exp(-2.062) / (1+exp(-2.062)) = 0.113



Shouldn't the coefficient for this ergm yield a

probability equal to the network density?



What am i missing?



Thanks

Brian

Based on your density calculations, I am assuming that this is an 

undirected graph?  In that case, you need to be sure to set 

directed=FALSE when creating your network object; the results you are 

now obtaining appear to be consistent with what you would expect for a 

digraph of order 105 with 1337 edges (which is what you'll get if you 

leave directed=TRUE).  Check this, and let us know if the issue persists.



BTW, it would be helpful if petitioners would 1) report the versions of 

R and the statnet packages they are using, and 2) include a short R 

script which will regenerate the problem.  Please do _not_ include large 

attachments (e.g., Rdata files), since this will flood readers' inboxes 

and anger various eldritch powers who must not be named.



Hope that helps,



-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ergm(net~edges) is not yielding density
messages.body_plain:
Hi Brian,



Thanks for the message. 



The problem appears to be that the network was created from a 
sociomatrix

with diagonal 1's. That is, all actors have self-ties, but the "loops" 
option to network is not set. Thus the network object is not stored in a 
self-consistent way.



To fix it you can do something like:



ta2.loops <- ta2[,]

diag(ta2.loops) <- 0

ta2.noloops <- network(ta2.loops, directed=F)



and then add the covariates back.



I hope this helps!



Mark
